user.title: Set up the Previous State Tracker
user.description: Select the entity for which you want to track the previous state.

data_description.name: Identifies this tracker under Settings > Devices & Services. The sensor's own display name is automatic -- it follows the tracked entity's name (and its device, if it has one), so it stays correct even if you rename that entity later.
data_description.ignore_extra_states: Pick from the entity's known/recent states (shown the same way the entity itself displays them), or type a new one. Only affects which state counts as the tracked entity's previous state -- it doesn't hide or filter the source entity itself.

reconfigure.title: Change the tracked entity
reconfigure.description: Change which entity "{name}" tracks. The sensor's name and options stay the same.

init.title: Adjust options for the Previous State Tracker

data_description.ignore_extra_states: Pick from the entity's known/recent states (shown the same way the entity itself displays them), or type a new one. Only affects which state counts as the tracked entity's previous state -- it doesn't hide or filter the source entity itself.

tracked_entity_removed.title: Tracked entity no longer exists
tracked_entity_removed.description: "{name}" is tracking `{entity_id}`, but that entity no longer exists (it may have been renamed or removed). The sensor will keep showing its last known value until you update it under Settings > Devices & Services > Previous State Tracker > Reconfigure.

tracked_entity_disabled.title: Tracked entity is disabled
tracked_entity_disabled.description: "{name}" is tracking `{entity_id}`, but that entity is currently disabled, so the sensor shows as unavailable. If that's intentional, you can dismiss this. Otherwise, re-enable the entity under Settings > Devices & Services > Entities.
